findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the boundary type-preservation requirement and the AST guard to reject {**boundary, ...} dict-unpacking (not only dict(...)), and add a seeded unpacking mutation to the RED-reversion coverage.
evidence: Context: three broad forms are 'dict(os.environ)', '{**os.environ, ...}', and 'os.environ.copy()' — dict-unpacking is explicitly one of them.
Plan guard clause names only 'dict(...) unwrapping of the boundary'; {**boundary, ...} unpacking is not named and equally collapses the boundary to a plain dict whose repr renders raw values.
Plan bullet 1 requires '.copy() preserves the boundary' — showing the author knows type-preservation matters — yet the same preservation requirement is not extended to dict-unpacking.
findings.finding: The redaction is only effective while the value stays the boundary type, but the plan's guard rejects only dict(...) unwrapping. The inventory itself lists {**os.environ, ...} dict-unpacking as one of the three broad forms; a developer writing {**BOUNDARY, 'K': 'v'} produces a plain dict with an un-redacted repr, an unguarded escape that re-exposes the exact leak the boundary is meant to prevent.
findings.location: Plan section bullet 4 ('rejects dict(...) unwrapping of the boundary'); AC line 'A seeded boundary-unwrapping mutation makes the AST guard fail'
scenarios: A new test writes env = {**SAFE_ENV, 'PATH': shim} and passes it to subprocess.run; on a startup failure the plain dict's repr leaks the retained ambient values, and the AST guard (only checking dict(...)) does not flag it.
findings.suggested_fix: Have .copy() and a dedicated .with_overrides(...) be the only sanctioned ways to derive a new mapping, and make the AST guard reject BOTH dict(<boundary>) and {**<boundary>, ...} as boundary-unwrapping, with a seeded {**boundary} mutation added to the boundary-unwrapping acceptance criterion.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a positive rationale for the retain-and-redact boundary over the sibling-proven explicit-allowlist approach (or adopt the allowlist), reconciling the direct conflict with dumbstruck-wonderful-xiphosuran's rejection of representation wrappers.
evidence: Sibling ticket 3402-7143-2e14-4d1a plan: 'Replace each broad ambient copy with an explicit mutable allowlist ... This is preferred over a representation wrapper because the subprocess contract itself should be explicit, the 24-test minimal-parent-environment run proves arbitrary keys are unnecessary, and it avoids adding a shared abstraction solely for test fixtures.'
tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py:149-158 already builds env from PATH + explicit STATE_DIR/DEPLOY_REPO/COMPOSE_DIR/MIRROR_DIR/HEALTH_TIMEOUT (allowlist), not a broad os.environ copy.

The plan gives no 'why this approach fits' sentence for the boundary; the boundary preserves 'exact inherited child environments', keeping arbitrary ambient values in the mapping the allowlist would have dropped entirely.
findings.finding: The plan chooses a repr-redacting dict 'boundary' that retains the full inherited environment, but the sibling ticket owning the seven cited fixtures (dumbstruck-wonderful-xiphosuran) explicitly evaluated and rejected this 'representation wrapper' in favor of an explicit allowlist, and the authoritative-contract target (test_autodeploy_review_drain.py) already uses the allowlist pattern. The plan states no positive rationale for choosing the wrapper over the established, sibling-proven allowlist approach.
findings.location: Plan section, bullets 1-2 ('Add a test-only mutable dict boundary whose representation redacts contents'); Test contract card authoritative_contract
scenarios: A reviewer or the sibling owner asks why two sibling tickets solve the identical leak class with opposite, mutually-inconsistent mechanisms (drop arbitrary keys vs. retain-but-redact).

A future leak carrier not covered by container repr (e.g. a stdlib frame that reprs a per-item string local) still exposes retained ambient values, whereas the allowlist would have had nothing sensitive to leak.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) adopt the sibling's explicit-allowlist mechanism for the 103 sites so both tickets converge on one proven pattern, or (b) add an explicit rationale explaining why the 103 test-local sites genuinely require retaining arbitrary inherited values (unlike the seven fixtures) such that an allowlist is infeasible and a redacting boundary is the minimal fit.

findings.checklist_item: Justify the novel redacting-mapping boundary against established prior art — cite pydantic SecretStr/Secret (already referenced in ADR 0098) and state why a mapping-level boundary is required (e.g., subprocess needs plain-string env values, so value-level secret wrapping cannot apply).
evidence: Plan: 'Add a test-only mutable dict boundary whose representation redacts contents, whose mapping behavior preserves exact inherited child environments, and whose .copy() preserves the boundary.'

Retrieved (pydantic docs): 'SecretStr : string where the value is kept partially secret. You can use ... for storing sensitive information that you do not want to be visible in logging or tracebacks' and 'subclass from a parametrized Secret to customize the str() and repr()'.

Repo ADR docs/adr/0098-operation-scoped-config-and-provider-composition.md:183 already states 'Pydantic SecretStr or SecretBytes. Pydantic masks normal' repr/logging — established in-repo prior art for redaction-on-repr.

ABSENCE: the plan contains no comparison to value-level secret wrappers and no Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging rationale for why a mapping-level boundary is required (e.g., that subprocess needs plain-string values so SecretStr cannot wrap individual env values).
findings.finding: The plan introduces a novel test-only mapping boundary that redacts its contents in __repr__ to prevent credential disclosure in tracebacks, but considers no prior art and does not justify the bespoke pattern against the established repr-redaction approach (pydantic SecretStr/Secret), which the repo's own ADR 0098 already cites as masking repr/logging.
findings.location: Plan section, bullet 1: 'Add a test-only mutable dict boundary whose representation redacts contents'
scenarios: Reviewer/maintainer asks why a bespoke redacting MutableMapping was built instead of reusing the repo's already-cited SecretStr pattern.
A future author extends redaction and cannot tell whether the established secret-type approach was rejected for a reason or simply overlooked.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short prior-art note to the Plan: reference pydantic SecretStr/Secret as the established repr-redaction pattern, and explain that because subprocess/_execute_child consumes a real string->string mapping, per-value secret wrapping is infeasible, hence a mapping-level boundary that redacts only in __repr__ while preserving exact values is the minimal necessary deviation.
